title: Heteroskedastic signal smoothing and warm-cohort playbook for autoscaler regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This ticket is the incident follow-up and action plan for a recent class of autoscaling regressions where heteroskedastic (bursty + noisy) traffic signals caused false positives and false negatives in the KEDA/HPA stack, producing both over-provisioning during transient spikes and under-provisioning during slow warmups. The event manifested as elevated tail latency on inference pods during mixed workload bursts and a sequence of cold-starts for warm cohorts. Goal: deliver a tested playbook that reduces spike-driven misfires, adds deterministic warm-cohort priming, and hardens probes and percentiles to reduce oscillation without regressing cost. Scope: tuning heuristics (percentile windows, holdoff, hysteresis), introducing a warm-cohort prewarm path, probe fusion (cross-metric smoothing), load-test suites, dashboards, and a canary rollout plan.
root_cause_summary: Noise amplification from a new probe weighting change combined with a shrinking percentile window in KEDA resulted in transient high-rate signals being interpreted as sustained demand. Simultaneous changes to our coldStartProbe timing exposed the cluster to delayed pod readiness which caused downstream perceived underprovisioning when burst tails arrived. The autoscaler lacked a warm-cohort priming mechanism, so newly created pods suffered cold-start latency at critical percentiles.
mitigation: Short-term: revert the probe-weight change and restore the previous percentile-window configuration (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2897). Apply a probe holdoff of 30s for new metrics and enable temporary scale headroom (10%) for high-traffic namespaces. Medium-term: deploy the smoothing circuit described below and add a warm-cohort priming controller (see action items).

action_items: A1: Implement 'heteroskedastic smoothing circuit' in runtime that blends percentile windows with an exponentially-weighted smoothing factor. Owner: Marco Reyes. ETA: 2026-03-17.
A2: Add warm-cohort priming controller that pre-initializes a small pool of pods per namespace when burst probability > threshold. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2026-03-24.
A3: Introduce probe fusion rule: fuse readiness, request-rate, and queue-length into a single scaled signal with holdoff. Owner: SRE (Jing Wu). ETA: 2026-03-15.
A4: Extend canary test harness with heteroskedastic workload generator and deterministic cold-start assertions; add to CI. Owner: QA (Evan Morris). ETA: 2026-03-18.
A5: Create a Grafana 'Autoscaler Resilience' dashboard with alerting thresholds and synthetic-run overlays. Owner: Observability (Rafael Ortiz). ETA: 2026-03-14.
A6: Run staged rollout: prod-canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 6-hour observation windows and rollback criteria. Owner: Releases (Hannah Li). ETA: rollout start 2026-03-19.
A7: Publish on-call playbook and runbook section for 'probe-noise incidents' with specific mitigation commands. Owner: Oncall Lead (Samir Kapoor). ETA: 2026-03-16.
tests_and_validation: We will validate changes with the synthetic heteroskedastic load harness (poisson baseline + burst spikes + gradual ramps). Acceptance criteria: 1) 95th pod startup latency improves by >=25% in burst test, 2) autoscaler flapping reduced to fewer than 1 scale event per 10-minute window during bursts, 3) cost delta < 6% during normal traffic in integration test.
rollout_plan: Canary sequence: merge to canary branch -> deploy to low-impact cluster -> run synthetic harness for 24h -> promote to 5% prod traffic -> monitor 6h windows with automated regress checks -> 25% -> 100%. Rollback on any regression in pod_startup_95th_latency or sustained tail latency (>50ms above baseline for 2 windows).
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs: smoothing reduces reactivity and may increase short-lived overprovisioning during genuine instant sustained traffic. To compensate we pair smoothing with warm-cohort priming and a short burst override for verified heavy sustained signals. Console UX change required to expose warm-cohort opt-in; tracked in PM backlog. Private deployments must opt-in due to RBAC/privilege surface.
